note: Every finding ever surfaced by the proactive bug scan (routine N2-A), keyed by fingerprint. Fingerprint = <path>#<enclosing symbol>#<bug class>. Never re-report a fingerprint whose state is reported, patched, wontfix or accepted.

findings.summary: The update-check rate limit is keyed on a persisted timestamp but guards an in-memory result, so a cold start inside the interval returns null for an update the app already knows about. The badge (persisted) advertises it while Settings -> Updates (in memory) shows nothing and the skip control is unreachable.

cancel() nulls the job before the coroutine has stopped, so isRunning under-reports while the cancelled run is still inside an in-flight request. Tapping the settings row again starts a second scan concurrently: the request pacing doubles and the plain LinkedHashSet 'unavailable' is mutated from two coroutines on Dispatchers.IO.
findings.not_patched_reason: Scored below the 80 patch bar, and the run's single code PR went to the higher-scoring finding.

findings.summary: The artwork-colour extraction launches into an outer coroutine scope from inside collectLatest, so collectLatest has nothing left to cancel. The launched work is never cancelled and its completions are unordered, so a stale song's colour can win and a colour can land after the user has switched dynamic theme off.
findings.not_patched_reason: Scored below the 80 patch bar, and the run's single code PR went to the higher-scoring finding.
findings.provenance_note: The collectLatest { scope.launch { } } shape is inherited verbatim from upstream's ui/theme/Theme.kt; the fork relocated it into MainActivity.kt during the theming rework. Filed because it now lives in our file and affects our users, not as a claim that the fork introduced it.

findings.summary: The catch-up progress predicate counts STATE_DOWNLOADING (epoch 1, meaning queued or in flight) as a landed download, because it only excludes null and STATE_INVALID. media3 fires onDownloadChanged with STATE_QUEUED as soon as a request is added, so the whole batch reads as done the moment enqueue finishes and the row jumps to "Downloaded N liked songs" before anything has been fetched. The same predicate cannot be tightened on its own: failed ids are removed from the map entirely (:736-739), so a completion-only count would never reach total and the coroutine would hang forever.
findings.not_patched_reason: Scored 64, below the 80 patch bar. A correct fix must restructure the progress collector to track completion and settlement together (>30 lines), and cannot be compiled or unit tested in this environment.
findings.introduced_by: c750adc1 (Show catch-up progress on the button, and let a second tap stop it)

findings.summary: The cancel path filters the download map for STATE_INVALID (epoch 0, failed) where it means STATE_DOWNLOADING (epoch 1, queued). Two consequences: none of the batch is actually removed, so media3 keeps downloading all of it after the user taps stop; and the entries that do match, which can only come from rescanDownloads reading epoch-0 dateDownload rows, are unrelated songs the user queued by hand. The function has no access to batch, so it also cannot distinguish the catch-up's downloads from anyone else's.
findings.not_patched_reason: Scored 68, below the 80 patch bar. Swapping the sentinel alone is also wrong (it would cancel manual downloads too), so the fix needs the batch lifted to a field; runtime-only verification.
findings.introduced_by: c750adc1 (Show catch-up progress on the button, and let a second tap stop it)

findings.summary: trip() recomputes the deadline as now + backoff on every call and its guard only refuses to shorten an existing stop, so any failing request during an active back off re-arms a fresh deadline (up to 20 minutes) from that moment. Playback is deliberately never gated, so a user retrying play on a refused network keeps pushing the deadline out and downloads, sync and scans stay disabled far longer than MAX_BACKOFF_MS. This contradicts the class's own stated invariant at Throttle.kt:39. Separately, strikes is incremented per call rather than per episode, so the documented 5/10/20 ladder is consumed within the first episode.
findings.not_patched_reason: Highest scorer of run 2 at 75, still below the 80 patch bar. Blast radius is small (an early return in trip), but Verifiability is capped at 6 because SystemClock and android.util.Log are framework calls and :app has no JVM unit-test source set.
findings.introduced_by: baa74f26 (Back off when YouTube refuses the network, and say so in words)

discarded.candidate: Conditional early return placed before a remember call (rememberPreference), which looked like a slot-table hazard.
discarded.reason: The Compose compiler supports early returns from composables by emitting group end markers, so the slot table stays consistent. No failure path.

discarded.candidate: 'while (isActive && pauseWhenSongEnd)' inside scope.launch, where the class also declares its own isActive property, so the two could be confused.
discarded.reason: Ambiguous to read but harmless. Kotlin resolves to CoroutineScope.isActive (an extension on the innermost implicit receiver beats a member of an outer one), and either reading terminates the loop correctly anyway.

discarded.candidate: 'checking' is not reset in a finally, so a throw from check() would leave the row permanently disabled.
discarded.reason: Real but the throw surface is only a DataStore IO error, and cancellation takes the whole composition with it. No concrete failure path worth an issue on its own.

discarded.candidate: The Throttle guard added in baa74f26 might cover only some of the three enqueue entry points, leaving the SyncUtils post-login backfill able to queue hundreds of requests at a refused network.
discarded.reason: All three paths are guarded: DownloadUtil.kt:286 (autoDownloadOnLike), :340 (startLikedDownloads) and :428 (downloadLikedSongs, which is the one SyncUtils.kt:211 calls).

discarded.candidate: result[s.song.id] = s.song.dateDownload!! force-unwraps a nullable column on rows drawn from downloadedOrQueuedSongs(), which by its name includes queued songs.
discarded.reason: The query is "SELECT * FROM song WHERE isLocal = 0 AND dateDownload IS NOT NULL" (SongsDao.kt:295), so the unwrap cannot fail. The inline comment "sql should cover our butts" is accurate.

discarded.candidate: gainProcessor.gain is set from normalizeFactor * playerVolume without the sleep-timer fade factor, so a fading-out track might keep full above-unity boost.
discarded.reason: The two stages are in series and disjoint: the processor passes through at or below unity, and player.volume carries min(total, 1f) * fadeFactor. The product is correct at every gain, so the fade still reaches silence.

discarded.candidate: Three GlobalScope.launch collectors are never cancelled.
discarded.reason: Application-scoped by intent: they collect DataStore for the life of the process, which is exactly GlobalScope's lifetime. No leak beyond process death, and no failure path.
